63: // diff compares two multi-line strings and returns a helpful comment
64: func diff(got, want string) string {
65: 	g := strings.Split(got, "\n")
66: 	w := strings.Split(want, "\n")
67: 	for i := 0; ; i++ {
68: 		switch {
69: 		case i < len(g) && i < len(w):
70: 			if g[i] == w[i] {
71: 				continue
72: 			}
73: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- first difference in line %d:\n"+
74: 				"-- got : %q\n-- want: %q\n", i+1, g[i], w[i])
75: 		case i < len(g):
76: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- got %d extra lines after line %d:\n"+
77: 				"-- first extra line: %q\n", len(g)-len(w), i, g[i])
78: 		case i < len(w):
79: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- got %d correct lines, want %d more lines:\n"+
80: 				"-- want next: %q\n", i, len(w)-i, w[i])
81: 		default:
82: 			return "no differences found"
83: 		}
84: 	}
85: }

Standard exercism food-chain. Implement it algorithmically.

Wait — the horse verse (v=8) ends with "She's dead, of course!" — in my code, after writing the comment, it returns b.String(), which includes the trailing newline after the comment. The expected text is:

```
I know an old lady who swallowed a horse.
She's dead, of course!
```

There's no trailing newline after "course!" — because the test compares exact strings. My code writes "She's dead, of course!\n" and then returns, so there's a trailing newline. This will fail.

Fix: don't add a newline after the comment when v==8. Let me restructure: write the comment without a newline when v==8, or trim the trailing newline.

Wait, but the fly verse (v=1) has no comment, so it falls through to the loop. The loop runs from i=1 to i>1, which never executes. Then it writes "I don't know why she swallowed the fly. Perhaps she'll die." — correct.

Now let's run the tests.

All tests pass. The implementation in `food_chain.go` builds the song algorithmically:

- **`Verse(v)`** — writes the opening line, then the per-animal comment (the horse verse ends there with `She's dead, of course!`), then walks the chain backwards: `She swallowed the X to catch the Y`, appending ` that wriggled and jiggled and tickled inside her` when the target is the spider, and closes with the fly line.
- **`Verses(start, end)`** — joins consecutive verses with a blank line.
- **`Song()`** — `Verses(1, 8)`.
